claim: Common ground is an ongoing process of grounding to a sufficient-for-current-purposes criterion, with cost set by the medium and by least collaborative effort.
schema_part: G/S: add a cheap grounding check when a message could be read two ways
agent_test: Ablate a 'restate my understanding and confirm' step vs none at equal tokens on underspecified tasks.
note: Human numbers added: Clark and Wilkes-Gibbs 41 to 8 words per figure over 6 trials; Brennan and Clark same vs new partner 48% vs 18%. Replication record still open (d09 unverified).

claim: Common-ground breakdown happens when one side assumes the other holds knowledge it lacks and does not know to ask; same word, different referent.
agent_test: Seed tasks with ambiguous terms (presentation=talk vs file); count wrong-referent actions with and without an explicit referent-gloss step.

claim: Addressees use common ground late, as a correction, not as an initial filter (egocentric default).
agent_test: Rival: spatial-coding account (Santiesteban 2015, director=camera accuracy .79 vs .80). Test only if agent plays referential tasks.
note: Gap 9: no LLM paper found testing the spatial-coding account. PARLEY authors report agents show excessive compliance instead of egocentric bias (d11).

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs presume common ground: 77.5% fewer grounding acts than humans (follow-ups -64.3%, acknowledgements -83.4%).
agent_test: Re-run Shaikh metrics on our agent with and without the scaffold at equal tokens.
note: Second source (Shaikh 2025 Rifts, same group, different data): LLMs 3x less likely to clarify, 16x less likely to follow up; 2024-era frontier models and o3-mini below chance. Same research group, so independence is partial; 2026 frontier models still untested.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Preference optimisation lowers grounding (DPO kappa falls, R about -0.79); SFT does not raise it; preference data rank questions lower (13.77% preferred vs 18.35% dispreferred).
agent_test: Check whether the scaffold's clarify step survives on a preference-tuned base model.

claim: Prompting a model to ground overshoots: follow-ups 10.76 to 42.32, but clarification kappa 0 to -1.65; frequency is fixed, timing is not.
schema_part: G (clarify only when ambiguity is detected)
agent_test: Compare always-ask vs ambiguity-gated asking: accuracy and number of questions at equal tokens.
note: A forecaster-gated prompt (decides when to ask) raised Rifts accuracy from about 24 to 54.48, so timing can be repaired with a gate (needs a trained forecaster).

claim: Models degrade a mean 39% when the task arrives in pieces over turns (aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%); causes are early assumptions and premature answers; recap only recovers part.
schema_part: S/O (hold assumptions as open; do not answer early)
agent_test: Shard benchmark items; measure scaffold vs plain with a rule 'no full answer until slots filled'.
note: Reasoning models (o3, R1) degrade similarly; recap on last turn recovers about 52% of lost points for GPT-4o, snowball about 18%; temperature 0 does not fix sharded unreliability. No equal-token test.

claim: Multi-agent systems fail often (41% to 86.7% across 7 frameworks); about 37% of failures are inter-agent misalignment.
agent_test: Not needed; use the taxonomy as a checklist for any multi-role internal step.

claim: Workflow and role fixes beat prompt fixes: +9.4% ChatDev success (attributed in paper to role specification and, elsewhere, to CEO final say) and +15.6% from added verification on ProgramDev.
agent_test: Add a final verification pass to a single-agent run; compare with an equal-token extra sample.
note: No replication of +9.4% found. Later work suggests role effects can come from a submission gate (recovery 0.198 to 0.613 when forcing submission).

claim: Multi-agent coordination helps on decomposable tasks (+80.8%) and hurts on sequential ones (-70.0%); independent agents amplify errors 17.2x vs 4.4x for centralised.
schema_part: none (supports staying single-agent for sequential work)
agent_test: Compare single agent vs internal role split on one sequential and one decomposable task at equal tokens.
note: 17.2 vs 4.4 confirmed as trace-level, relative to single agent = 1.0 by definition; error amplification coefficient not significant after controls (p=0.658). Not evidence about single-agent verifiers.

claim: Multi-agent debate often fails to beat chain of thought or self-consistency at higher cost.
agent_test: Equal-token compare debate vs self-consistency on our benchmarks.

claim: Human-AI teams on average do worse than the best of human or AI alone (g=-0.23); decision tasks lose (g=-0.27), creation tasks gain (g=+0.19, ns).
agent_test: Where our agent hands off to a human, test whether the human step helps on decisions.

claim: Letting the human or agent act at any time with notifications beat strict turn-taking; human-agent collaboration beat autonomous agents (win 86/74/66%), yet communication failures stay at 65%.
agent_test: Only relevant for interactive deployment.

claim: Training for multi-turn rewards makes models ask and clarify: +18.5% task performance, +46.3% interactivity, user study +17.6% satisfaction.
agent_test: Prompt-only imitation of the behaviour at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit belief-state text improves LLM teamwork and theory-of-mind probe accuracy (GPT-4 1st-order 60.0 to 80.1; 2nd-order 64.3 to 69.4).
agent_test: Add a 'what the other party believes/knows' field; compare with none at equal tokens.
note: Li 2023 round-count gain (28.3 vs 12.3) unverifiable from table text; use ToM probe accuracy and valid-action gains only. Grounding Layer (explicit status slot) supports a slot in a single agent.

claim: LLM theory-of-mind success is brittle: tiny changes (transparent bag) keep 95 to 98% on the wrong answer; belief tracking in conversations is far below humans (FANToM human 87.5, GPT-4 CoT 14.8 to 26.6).
schema_part: G (do not trust surface fluency about others' beliefs)
agent_test: Run FANToM-style asymmetric information items with and without a belief ledger.

claim: LLM agents are strong at coordination solved from world state and weak at modelling partners; joint planning and ToM trail environment comprehension (Hanabi GPT-4-turbo 13.33 vs RL 24).
agent_test: Not needed.

claim: Seeing the partner's view raises accuracy but makes models over-predict shared understanding (aligned recall .590 to .822).
agent_test: MapTask-style alignment labels with and without visibility of partner view.
note: Related: clarifying questions raise perceived understanding while cutting user scrutiny (N=180).

claim: Shared mental models predict team process and performance (rho=.35, 128 studies, 2017; r=.29 on performance, 2010); effect depends on measurement method and on compositional vs compilational emergence.
agent_test: Analogy only; not directly testable.

claim: Self-play agents form private conventions that fail with new partners; symmetry-breaking training gives 15.75 vs 9.15 with human partners.
agent_test: Check if the agent's own conventions (labels) confuse a fresh reader.

claim: A shared-board (blackboard) design beats CoT by 4.33% and static multi-agent by 5.02% on average.
agent_test: Single-agent scratch ledger vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Formal common-ground tracking in group tasks is feasible but weak: move F1 0.61, common ground F1 0.54; LLMs infer group beliefs poorly (Dice 0.219 to 0.382).
agent_test: Not needed.

claim: A separate ambiguity check that decides when to ask matches forced-ask and fully specified performance on underspecified coding tasks (69.4 vs 70.4 vs 70.8 resolve rate) and beats never-ask (54.8); one agent self-checking reaches only 61.2.
schema_part: G (clarify only when ambiguity is detected); separate check step
agent_test: Equal-token test: never-ask vs always-ask vs gated ask on underspecified tasks, report tokens and questions per task.

claim: Models rarely detect that a task is underspecified (some at 50% chance; best 84-89%), but use answers well once asked (up to 74% gain); detection is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Measure detector accuracy alone on a seeded ambiguous set.

claim: LLMs do not form partner-specific conceptual pacts or shorten references over rounds, unlike humans (41 to 8 words per figure over 6 trials in Clark and Wilkes-Gibbs); they succeed by verbose description.
agent_test: Check if a term ledger reduces re-description and wrong-referent errors across a long session.

claim: Clarifying questions can raise false trust: users accept more erroneous answers and review less after being asked questions (N=180).
schema_part: G (do not treat having asked as aligned)
agent_test: None needed for the agent; keep as a design caution.

claim: No measured test of Klein et al. Basic Compact requirements (predictability, directability) on LLM teammates was found; closest evidence is descriptive failure taxonomies (695 incidents, 163,487 posts) and a common-ground benchmark.
agent_test: None; background only.

claim: An explicit status record of what has been agreed (accepted, unacknowledged, revised, scoped) raises correct action choice in single agents (Sensitivity 0.06 to 0.56 DeepSeek, 0.13 to 0.49 Qwen), and more user information alone can raise execution of unacknowledged proposals.
agent_test: Single-agent agreement ledger vs none on tasks with unconfirmed proposals.
